title: Amadeus: When Models of People Meet
abstract: arXiv:2609.35835v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: With the sheer constant advancements raining down in the field of Artificial Intelligence, one particular possibility that may cross our mind is whether it is possible to model agents after humans and, in turn, use these agents to carry out synthetic interactions that predict their real counterparts, or even interactions at a larger scale such as groups or societies. In this paper, we test a more controlled version of this question through chess. We use 8 elite chess players, seal their direct pairwise games, learn each player independently using different methods, and then compose the resulting models on the withheld dyads. To evaluate the generated interactions, we use two measurements: opening-family total variation distance and win-draw-loss (WDL) total variation distance. M1 reduces WDL-TV while leaving opening-family TV largely unchanged, whereas M2 substantially reduces opening-family TV while having little effect on WDL-TV. An

translated_abstract: 随着人工智能领域的不断进步，我们可能会想到这样一个问题：是否可以模仿人类来构建智能体模型，进而利用这些智能体开展合成交互，以预测真实人类之间的交互，甚至是更大规模的交互，例如群体或社会层面。在本文中，我们通过国际象棋对这一问题的更可控版本进行了测试。我们选取8名精英国际象棋棋手，封存他们之间的直接对弈棋局，使用不同方法独立学习每位棋手的建模，然后将被保留的配对对局用于组合生成的模型。为了评估生成的交互，我们采用了两个度量指标：开局家族总变差距离和胜负和（WDL）总变差距离。M1降低了WDL-TV，而开局家族TV基本保持不变；而M2则大幅降低了开局家族TV，但对WDL-TV几乎没有影响。
tldr: 本文以国际象棋为可控实验场景，通过独立建模8名精英棋手并让其模型进行配对对弈，证明了基于人类建模的智能体能够在开局风格和胜负和分布两个维度上逼近真实的人类对局交互。
